subject: chemistry
question_text: Draw the shape of a d orbital.

verification.note: Chapter 1 is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.48-52), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. FIGURE SCOPE: the book draws all five d orbitals. This card draws the two DIFFERENT shapes — the four-lobed one that four of them share, and the distinct dz² — and names all five in the second step, because five small sketches on one page are not legible.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The diagram
steps.why: Four of the five d orbitals share one shape, the four-lobed double dumb-bell, so drawing it once shows the shape the question asks for. The dz² orbital is drawn separately because it is the one that looks different.
common_mistakes: Drawing a two-lobed dumb-bell. That is a p orbital, not a d orbital.
Leaving the ring off dz². The ring in the xy plane is what makes it a d orbital.
steps.memory_tip: A d orbital has four lobes, twice as many as a p orbital. Only dz² is different.
steps.margin_note: One clear four-lobed sketch is enough. Add dz² if there is room.

steps.label: The five d orbitals
lines: dxy, dyz, dzx lie between the axes.
dx²−y² lies along the x and y axes.
dz² has two lobes along z and a ring in
Shape: double dumb-bell. Each has 2 nodal planes.
steps.why: For d orbitals l = 2, so m takes five values and there are five orbitals. Four of them are four-lobed and differ only in how they sit relative to the axes; dz² is the fifth and the odd one.
common_mistakes: Writing that there are three d orbitals. Three is the count for p.
Saying all five have the same shape. dz² has a ring the others do not.
steps.memory_tip: Three between the axes, one along the axes, and dz² on its own. That is five.
steps.margin_note: Naming all five with l = 2 earns this mark even if only one shape is drawn.

insider_note: The question says shape, singular, so one good four-lobed drawing carries the diagram mark. The five names and l = 2 are what complete the answer.
